issues.failure_explanation: The two-stage Runge-Kutta form is not the stated scheme/Radau IIA method: the stage derivatives must satisfy k_i=f(...)-A(u_T(t_T)+|T| sum_j a_ij k_j). As written, for f=0 and A=lambda I the stage system is homogeneous and gives k_1=k_2=0, hence u_T(t_{T+1})=u_T(t_T) for every lambda and |T|, contradicting the damping endpoint factor computed for the actual scheme in eq:qeval.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the stage equations as k_1=f(t_T+|T|/3)-A(u_T(t_T)+|T|(5 k_1/12-k_2/12)) and k_2=f(t_{T+1})-A(u_T(t_T)+|T|(3 k_1/4+k_2/4)), keeping the same update weights.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed classical time-stepping implementation is inconsistent with the analyzed Petrov-Galerkin scheme and with Radau IIA; an implementation based on this display would not damp the lambda-mode. The later inf-sup/optimality analysis uses the Petrov-Galerkin formulation, so it is not itself built on this display.
issues.title: Classical Radau update omits the current state in the stage equations
issues.why_classification: The repair is a direct correction of one displayed computational formula and preserves the analyzed scheme and all formal guarantees; no proof architecture or rate changes.

However, due to Lemma~\ref{lem:reliability}, both quantities are equivalent.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated under the model-problem assumption f in L^2(0,t_end;V^*), but the estimator already differentiates f and the optimality proof equates the error and estimator approximation classes through Lemma lem:reliability, which is only assumed for f in S^2(TT;V^*). The efficiency part also uses a polynomial inverse inequality for the residual; no data-oscillation term is included. Thus the proof applies a key lemma outside its stated hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Let $V$ be finite dimensional and let the initial mesh $\TT_0$ be uniform. Moreover, let the marking parameter $0<\theta\leq 1$ be sufficiently small, and let the grading parameter $G\in\N$ be sufficiently large.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis f in S^2(TT_0;V^*) (equivalently f remains piecewise quadratic on every trisection refinement) to Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping and to the downstream results using its setting, or else augment the estimator and approximation class with data oscillation and prove the corresponding reliability/efficiency statements. The least source-supported repair is the added hypothesis already isolated in Lemma lem:reliability.
issues.overall_effect: Rate optimality is not established for general L^2 right-hand sides as stated. The model-order-reduction error theorems that say they are in the setting of Theorem thm:optimal_timestepping inherit the same unsupported scope for the time-discretization error/estimator terms.
issues.title: Main optimality theorem omits the right-hand-side regularity used by the estimator theory
issues.why_classification: The fix is contained and uses an assumption already present in the paper, so no new optimality architecture is needed; but it narrows the advertised right-hand-side regime rather than being a purely local degenerate-case correction.

issues.failure_explanation: With gamma=lambda|T_0|, eq:qeval gives |q_{T_0}(t_1)|=2|3-gamma|/(gamma^2+4 gamma+6), which is asymptotic to 2/gamma for large gamma, not <=1/(4 gamma). For example gamma=10 gives |q|=14/146>1/40. The proof only needs the true uniform bound gamma |q(gamma)|^2<=C(gamma_0) for gamma>=gamma_0, but the stated stronger inequality is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false pointwise inequality by the uniform consequence of eq:qeval: for gamma=lambda|T_0|>=gamma_0, lambda|T_0| |q_{T_0}(t_1)|^2 = gamma |q(gamma)|^2 <= C(gamma_0), and then estimate lambda|T_0| |f_{T_0}(t_1)|^2 <= C(gamma_0)|u(I_i^-)|^2.
issues.overall_effect: The large-time-step inf-sup proof contains an invalid estimate; as written, the scalar inf-sup lemma and the results built on uniform inf-sup stability are not supported by the displayed argument, although the needed consequence follows from the same explicit formula.
issues.title: False pointwise decay bound for the invisible Radau mode
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local replacement of one rational-function bound by a uniform bound already implied by the same display; the lemma statement, constant selection strategy, rate, and downstream proof architecture are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The quantity epsilon(V_R) is a sum of squared Hardy-space norms. For the Laplace transform on Re s=alpha, the Paley-Wiener isometry uses the time weight e^{-2 alpha t}; since e^{-2 alpha t}>=e^{-2 alpha t_end} on [0,t_end], the squared time-domain projection error is bounded by e^{2 alpha t_end} epsilon(V_R), not by e^{alpha t_end} epsilon(V_R). Data concentrated near t=t_end show that the displayed factor is generally too small for alpha t_end>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace e^{alpha t_end} by e^{2 alpha t_end} in the squared estimate in eq:eps_V_R_Laplace, equivalently state the unsquared bound with factor e^{alpha t_end} sqrt(epsilon(V_R)).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed justification for the reduced-basis goal functional is false as written. After taking square roots, the correct squared estimate still yields the e^{alpha t_end} factor appearing in the exponential-convergence theorem, but the stated squared inequality itself is invalid.
issues.title: Wrong exponential weight in the Paley-Wiener projection estimate
issues.why_classification: Only one exponential factor in a squared estimate must be corrected; the subsequent unsquared exponential factor and the convergence rates remain the same, so no substantive guarantee is lost.
